Skill profiles of professions in two windows

Source: R/emerging_profession.R
build_profile_pair.Rd

Builds the sparse skill profiles of each profession in a base and a target window, the input of the profile-change functions.

Usage

build_profile_pair(
  panel,
  prof_col,
  skill_col = "skill_id",
  time_col = "mese_idx",
  x_col = "x",
  n_col = "n",
  base,
  target
)

Arguments

panel

Profession-level share panel (e.g. from compute_share_panel() with group_cols = prof_col).

prof_col

Profession column.

skill_col

Skill column. Default "skill_id".

time_col, x_col, n_col

See compute_share_trend().

base, target

Numeric vectors c(from, to) with the bounds of the base and target windows.

Value

An object of class skillviz_profile_pair: a list with a and b (sparse dgCMatrix, skills x professions, base and target shares), n_a and n_b (named postings per profession), and the metadata prof_col, skill_col, base, target.

Details

For profession \(j\) and window \(W\), the profile entry of skill \(k\) is the share of the profession's postings that mention the skill, \(s_{kj} = \sum_{t \in W} x_{kjt} / \sum_{t \in W} n_{jt}\). The denominator of a profession-period must be the same on all its rows. Only professions with postings in both windows are kept; the skill universe is the union of skills with a positive count in either window.

Examples

panel <- data.table::data.table(
  cp4 = "p1", skill_id = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 2),
  mese_idx = rep(1:2, each = 3), x = c(50, 50, 0, 50, 0, 50), n = 100
)
pair <- build_profile_pair(panel, "cp4", base = c(1, 1), target = c(2, 2))
pair$a
#> 3 x 1 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>    p1
#> a 0.5
#> b 0.5
#> c .
